p.src: Now Yuan Shao raised his army and advanced toward Guandu. Xiahou Dun sent an urgent dispatch asking for aid. Cao Cao mustered seventy thousand troops and went to meet the enemy, leaving Xun Yu to defend the capital at Xu. As Yuan Shao's army was about to depart, Tian Feng submitted a remonstrance from prison: “For the present, we should hold our ground and await Heaven's time. We must not recklessly launch a great army, lest misfortune follow.” Feng Ji slandered him, saying, “My lord has raised an army of benevolence and justice. How dare Tian Feng utter such ill-omened words?”

p.src: Yuan Shao flew into a rage and wanted to execute Tian Feng. The assembled officers pleaded for his life. Yuan Shao said bitterly, “Once I have defeated Cao Cao, I shall formally punish his crime!” He then pressed his army to advance. Banners covered the fields, and swords and spears stood thick as a forest. Upon reaching Yangwu, they established a fortified camp. Ju Shou said, “Though our forces are numerous, they do not match the enemy in valor; though their troops are elite, their provisions do not equal ours. Because they lack provisions, their advantage lies in a swift battle; because we have provisions, we should hold patiently for now. If we can prolong matters over the months, their army will collapse without a battle.” Yuan Shao angrily replied, “Tian Feng has already weakened my army's spirit; when I return, I shall certainly execute him. How dare you say the same!” He ordered his attendants to put Ju Shou in chains and confine him within the army. “After I have defeated Cao Cao, I shall punish him together with Tian Feng!” He then ordered his seven hundred thousand troops to encamp in every direction, their linked camps extending for more than ninety li.

p.src: Scouts learned the true state of affairs and carried their report to Guandu. Cao Cao's troops had only just arrived, and all were frightened by the news. Cao Cao conferred with his advisers. Xun You said, “Though Yuan Shao's army is large, it is nothing to fear. Our troops are all elite warriors, each capable of facing ten foes. But our advantage lies in a swift battle. If the struggle drags on for months and our provisions prove insufficient, there will be cause for grave concern.” Cao Cao said, “Your words accord exactly with my thoughts.” He therefore ordered his troops to advance with a great clamor. Yuan Shao's army came out to meet them, and both sides drew up their battle lines. Shen Pei stationed ten thousand crossbowmen in ambush on the two wings; he concealed five thousand archers behind the main standard, with orders to shoot together at the agreed signal.

p.src: After the drums had sounded three times, Yuan Shao, wearing a golden helmet and armor, a brocade robe, and a jade belt, reined his horse before the lines. At his sides stood his generals Zhang He, Gao Lan, Han Meng, Chunyu Qiong, and others. The banners, insignia, and ceremonial axes were arrayed in imposing order. When the main standard parted in Cao Cao's formation, Cao Cao rode forth. Xu Chu, Zhang Liao, Xu Huang, Li Dian, and the others, each bearing his weapon, guarded him before and behind. Pointing his whip at Yuan Shao, Cao Cao said, “Before the Son of Heaven, I recommended you for appointment as General-in-Chief. Why do you now plot rebellion?” Yuan Shao angrily replied, “You bear the name of Han chancellor, but in truth you are a traitor to the Han! Your crimes reach to Heaven and surpass those of Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo, yet you falsely accuse another of rebellion!” Cao Cao said, “I now obey the imperial edict and come to punish you!” Yuan Shao said, “I obey the Girdle Edict and come to punish the traitor!”

p.src: Enraged, Cao Cao sent Zhang Liao out to fight. Zhang He spurred his horse forward to meet him. The two generals fought for forty or fifty bouts without either gaining the advantage. Watching them, Cao Cao secretly marveled. Xu Chu brandished his saber, spurred his horse, and charged straight out to assist. Gao Lan leveled his spear and intercepted him. The four generals paired off and fought fiercely. Cao Cao ordered Xiahou Dun and Cao Hong each to lead three thousand troops and charge the enemy formation together. When Shen Pei saw Cao Cao's troops charging the lines, he ordered the signal cannon fired. Ten thousand crossbows discharged from both flanks, while the archers at the center surged before the lines and shot in a wild volley. Unable to withstand them, Cao Cao's troops fled southward in haste. Yuan Shao drove his troops forward in pursuit. Cao Cao's army suffered a crushing defeat and retreated entirely to Guandu. Yuan Shao moved his army closer to Guandu and encamped. Shen Pei said, “We can now detach a hundred thousand troops to hold Guandu and build earthen hills before Cao Cao's camp, so our soldiers may look down into it and shoot arrows. If Cao Cao abandons this place and withdraws, we shall gain this strategic pass, and Xuchang can be taken.”

p.src: Yuan Shao followed this counsel. He selected strong, able soldiers from every camp, equipped them with iron spades and earth-carrying poles, and sent them together to Cao Cao's camp, where they heaped earth into hills. Seeing Yuan Shao's troops building earthen hills, the men in Cao Cao's camp sought to rush out and attack, but Shen Pei's bowmen and crossbowmen blocked every vital passage, so they could not advance. Within ten days, more than fifty earthen hills were completed. High platforms were raised upon them, and detachments of bowmen and crossbowmen were stationed there to shoot. Cao Cao's soldiers were greatly frightened and defended themselves with arrow-shields held over their heads. Whenever a wooden clapper sounded from the earthen hills, arrows fell like rain. Cao Cao's troops crouched on the ground beneath their shields, while Yuan Shao's men shouted and laughed. Seeing his troops in disorder, Cao Cao assembled his advisers and asked for a plan. Liu Ye stepped forward and said, “We can build stone-throwing carts to destroy them.” Cao Cao ordered Liu Ye to submit a design. Several hundred stone-throwing carts were built overnight and deployed inside the camp walls, directly facing the high platforms on the earthen hills. Whenever the enemy bowmen began shooting, the men within the camp hauled the stone-throwing carts all at once, sending rocks flying through the air to batter the heights. There was nowhere to hide, and countless bowmen were killed. Yuan Shao's troops called these machines “Thunderclap Carts.”

p.src: Thereafter Yuan Shao's troops no longer dared climb the heights to shoot. Shen Pei then proposed another plan: he ordered soldiers to dig secret tunnels with iron spades, leading straight into Cao Cao's camp, and called them the “Tunneling Corps.” Cao Cao's soldiers saw Yuan Shao's men digging pits behind the hills and reported it to Cao Cao. Cao Cao again asked Liu Ye for counsel. Liu Ye said, “Unable to attack openly, Yuan Shao's troops are attacking in secret. They are digging concealed passages in hopes of entering the camp from underground.” Cao Cao asked, “How can we defend against it?” Liu Ye replied, “Dig a long trench around the camp, and their hidden tunnels will be useless.” That very night, Cao Cao assigned troops to dig the trench. When Yuan Shao's tunnels reached the trench, they could indeed go no farther, and all their labor was wasted.

p.src: Cao Cao was overjoyed upon receiving the letter and ordered his officers and men to exert themselves and defend the position to the death. Yuan Shao's army withdrew some thirty li, and Cao Cao sent a general out of camp on patrol. Shi Huan, a subordinate general under Xu Huang, captured one of Yuan Shao's scouts and brought him before Xu Huang. Xu Huang questioned him about the true condition of the army. The scout replied, “Sooner or later, General Han Meng will bring provisions to supply the army at the front. We were sent ahead to reconnoiter the road.” Xu Huang promptly reported the matter to Cao Cao. Xun You said, “Han Meng possesses no more than the courage of a common brute. If we send one man with several thousand light cavalry to strike him midway and cut off the provisions, Yuan Shao's army will fall into disorder of itself.” Cao Cao asked, “Who can undertake it?” Xun You replied, “Send Xu Huang.”

p.src: Cao Cao therefore ordered Xu Huang to take Shi Huan and their troops ahead, then sent Zhang Liao and Xu Chu with soldiers to support them. That night, Han Meng escorted several thousand provision carts toward Yuan Shao's camp. As they were traveling, Xu Huang and Shi Huan led their troops out from a mountain valley and blocked the road. Han Meng galloped forward to fight. Xu Huang engaged him in combat, while Shi Huan scattered the transport laborers and set fire to the provision carts. Unable to hold his ground, Han Meng wheeled his horse and fled. Xu Huang urged his troops on until all the baggage and supplies had been burned. In Yuan Shao's army, men saw flames rising in the northwest. While they were still startled and uncertain, routed troops arrived with the report: “The provisions have been seized.”

Just as they were about to engage, Zhang Liao's and Xu Chu's troops arrived behind them. Attacked from both sides, Yuan Shao's troops were scattered. The four generals joined forces and returned to the camp at Guandu. Cao Cao was delighted and rewarded them handsomely; he also detached troops to establish another camp before the main one, forming mutually supporting positions.

p.src: Now Han Meng returned to camp with his defeated troops. Yuan Shao was furious and intended to execute him, but the officers pleaded for mercy. Shen Pei said, “In warfare, provisions are of the utmost importance and must be guarded with the greatest care. Wuchao is our supply depot and must be defended by a strong force.” Yuan Shao replied, “My plans are already settled. Return to Ye and oversee the provisions; see that there is no shortage.” Shen Pei accepted the command and departed. Yuan Shao dispatched the general Chunyu Qiong with his subordinate commanders Sui Yuanjin, Han Juzi, Lü Weihuang, Zhao Rui, and others, leading twenty thousand troops to defend Wuchao. Chunyu Qiong was harsh by nature and fond of wine, and the soldiers mostly feared him; once at Wuchao, he spent every day drinking with his officers.

p.src: Meanwhile, Cao Cao’s provisions were nearly exhausted. He urgently sent a messenger to Xuchang, ordering Xun Yu to procure supplies without delay and send them by forced marches to relieve the army at the front. The messenger departed bearing the letter; but before he had gone thirty li, Yuan Shao’s soldiers captured him, bound him, and brought him before the adviser Xu You. Xu You, whose courtesy name was Ziyuan, had been Cao Cao’s friend in his youth, but was now serving Yuan Shao as an adviser. When the messenger was searched, Cao Cao’s letter pressing for supplies was found upon him. Xu You went straight to Yuan Shao and said, “Cao Cao has long been encamped at Guandu, locked in a standoff with us, so Xuchang must be undefended. If we detach a force to make a surprise night attack on Xuchang, the city can be taken and Cao Cao captured. Now that Cao Cao’s supplies are exhausted, we should seize this opportunity and strike him from both directions.” Yuan Shao said, “Cao Cao is exceedingly crafty. This letter is a ruse to lure us out.” Xu You replied, “If we do not take it now, we shall suffer for it later.”

p.src: While they were speaking, a messenger suddenly arrived from Ye Commandery and presented a letter from Shen Pei. The letter first discussed the transport of provisions; then it reported that while Xu You was in Jizhou, he had often unlawfully accepted property from the people and had allowed his sons and nephews to levy excessive taxes and provisions for their own gain; his sons and nephews had now been arrested and imprisoned. On reading the letter, Yuan Shao flew into a rage and cried, “You lawless wretch! How dare you still show your face before me and offer counsel! You have old ties with Cao Cao. I suppose he has bribed you as well, and you are acting as his spy to trick my army! You deserve to be beheaded, but for now I shall leave your head upon your shoulders! Leave at once, and never appear before me again!”

p.src: Xu You came out, looked up to heaven, and sighed, “Loyal counsel grates upon the ear; that fool is not worth advising! My sons and nephews have already fallen victim to Shen Pei. How can I ever face the people of Jizhou again?” He then drew his sword, intending to cut his own throat. Those around him wrested the sword away and remonstrated, “Why, sir, do you hold your life so cheap? Yuan Shao refuses to heed honest counsel; in the end he will surely be captured by Cao Cao. Since you have old ties with Lord Cao, why not leave darkness and turn to the light?” These few words awakened Xu You; and so he went straight over to Cao Cao. A later poet lamented this in verse:

p.src: Now Xu You slipped secretly out of camp and went straight to Cao Cao’s encampment, where the soldiers guarding the approaches seized him. Xu You said, “I am an old friend of Chancellor Cao. Report me at once and say that Xu You of Nanyang has come to see him.” The soldiers hurried into the camp to report. Cao Cao had just removed his clothes to rest. When he heard that Xu You had deserted privately to his camp, he was overjoyed and rushed barefoot to welcome him, without even taking time to put on his shoes. Seeing Xu You from afar, he clapped his hands and laughed with delight, took him by the hand, and entered with him; then Cao Cao bowed to the ground first. Xu You hastily helped him up and said, “You are Chancellor of the Han, while I am but a commoner. Why show me such humility and courtesy?” Cao Cao replied, “You are my old friend. How could I dare rank us by titles and honors?” Xu You said, “I failed to choose my lord wisely and humbled myself beneath Yuan Shao. He would neither hear my words nor follow my plans, so now I have left him expressly to visit an old friend. I beg you to take me into your service.” Cao Cao said, “Ziyuan, now that you are willing to join me, my cause is assured. Pray instruct me at once in a plan to defeat Yuan Shao.” Xu You said, “I once advised Yuan Shao to send light cavalry against the undefended capital of Xu, attacking you from front and rear.” Cao Cao exclaimed in alarm, “Had Yuan Shao followed your advice, my cause would have been lost.” Xu You asked, “How much provision does your army now have?” Cao Cao replied, “Enough for a year.” Xu You laughed. “I doubt it.” Cao Cao said, “Only half a year, then.”

p.src: Xu You rose with a sweep of his sleeves and strode out of the tent, saying, “I came to you in sincerity, yet you deceive me so. This is hardly what I expected!” Cao Cao held him back and said, “Ziyuan, do not be angry. Allow me now to tell you the truth. In truth, the army has only enough grain for three months.” Xu You laughed and said, “All men call Mengde a crafty hero; now I see it is true.” Cao Cao also laughed. “Have you not heard that in war no deception is too base?” Then he whispered in Xu You’s ear, “The army has only enough grain for this month.” Xu You cried aloud, “Do not deceive me! Your grain is already exhausted!” Cao Cao said in astonishment, “How do you know?” Xu You produced Cao Cao’s letter to Xun Yu and showed it to him. “Who wrote this letter?” Cao Cao asked in alarm, “Where did you obtain it?” Xu You told him how the messenger had been captured. Cao Cao took his hand and said, “Ziyuan, since you have come out of regard for our old friendship, I beg you to instruct me.” Xu You said, “My lord, you oppose a mighty enemy with a lone army, yet seek no means of winning quickly. That is the path to destruction. I have a plan that, within three days, will make Yuan Shao’s army of a million collapse without a battle. Are you still willing to listen?” Cao Cao said joyfully, “I should be glad to hear your excellent plan.” Xu You said, “All Yuan Shao’s provisions and baggage are stored at Wuchao, which he has now assigned Chunyu Qiong to guard. u.src: Xu You rose with a sweep of his sleeves and strode out of the tent, saying, “I came to you in sincerity, yet you deceive me so. This is hardly what I expected!”
Cao Cao held him back and said, “Ziyuan, do not be angry. Allow me now to tell you the truth.
In truth, the army has only enough grain for three months.”
Xu You laughed and said, “All men call Mengde a crafty hero; now I see it is true.”
Cao Cao also laughed. “Have you not heard that in war no deception is too base?”
Then he whispered in Xu You’s ear, “The army has only enough grain for this month.”
Xu You cried aloud, “Do not deceive me! Your grain is already exhausted!”
Cao Cao said in astonishment, “How do you know?”
Xu You produced Cao Cao’s letter to Xun Yu and showed it to him. “Who wrote this letter?”
Cao Cao asked in alarm, “Where did you obtain it?”
Xu You told him how the messenger had been captured.
Cao Cao took his hand and said, “Ziyuan, since you have come out of regard for our old friendship, I beg you to instruct me.”
Xu You said, “My lord, you oppose a mighty enemy with a lone army, yet seek no means of winning quickly. That is the path to destruction.

p.src: The next day, Cao Cao personally selected five thousand cavalry and infantry and prepared to raid the grain stores at Wuchao. Zhang Liao said, “How could Yuan Shao’s supply depot be left unguarded? You must not go there rashly, Chancellor. I fear Xu You may be deceiving us.” Cao Cao replied, “No. Xu You’s coming here means that Heaven intends Yuan Shao’s defeat. Our army now lacks provisions and cannot hold out for long. If we do not use Xu You’s plan, we shall merely sit and wait to be overwhelmed. If he meant treachery, why would he consent to remain in my camp? Besides, I have long wished to raid their camp. This raid upon their provisions must be carried out. Do not doubt it.” Zhang Liao said, “We must also guard against Yuan Shao attacking while our camp is weakened.” Cao Cao laughed. “I have already considered it thoroughly.” He ordered Xun You, Jia Xu, and Cao Hong to remain with Xu You in defense of the main camp; Xiahou Dun and Xiahou Yuan were to lead one force in ambush on the left, while Cao Ren and Li Dian led another in ambush on the right, ready for any unforeseen event. He placed Zhang Liao and Xu Chu in the vanguard, Xu Huang and Yu Jin in the rear, and himself in the center with the other generals. The five thousand troops carried Yuan Shao’s banners; every soldier bound grass and bore firewood upon his back. With gags between the men’s teeth and the horses’ mouths restrained, they set out for Wuchao at dusk. That night the sky was filled with stars.

p.src: Now Ju Shou, held under guard in Yuan Shao's army, saw the stars shining brightly arrayed that night and ordered his jailer to lead him into the courtyard, where he raised his eyes to observe the heavens. Suddenly he saw Venus moving retrograde and trespassing upon the celestial divisions of Ox and Dipper. Greatly alarmed, he cried, “Disaster is near!” That very night, he therefore begged for an audience with Yuan Shao. Yuan Shao was already lying drunk, but when told that Ju Shou had a secret matter to report, he summoned him and asked what it was. Ju Shou said, “I have just observed the heavens. Venus was moving retrograde between Willow and Ghost, and its streaming light shot into the divisions of Ox and Dipper. I fear we shall suffer a raid by enemy troops. Wuchao is where our grain is stored; we cannot fail to take precautions. You should swiftly dispatch picked troops and valiant generals to patrol the byways and mountain roads, lest Cao Cao outwit us.” Yuan Shao angrily rebuked him: “You are a condemned man! How dare you speak recklessly and mislead the army?” Then he berated the jailer: “I ordered you to keep him imprisoned. How dare you let him out?” He ordered the jailer beheaded and summoned another man to keep Ju Shou in custody. As Ju Shou withdrew, he covered his face and wept, sighing, “Our army's destruction is but hours away, and I know not where my bones will lie!” A later poet lamented this in verse:

p.src: Meanwhile, Cao Cao led his troops onward by night. As they passed one of Yuan Shao's outlying camps, its soldiers demanded to know whose force they were. Cao Cao had a man answer, “Jiang Qi has been ordered to Wuchao to protect the grain.” Seeing their own army's banners, Yuan Shao's soldiers entertained no suspicion. At every post they passed, they falsely claimed to be Jiang Qi's troops and met no obstruction. By the time they reached Wuchao, the fourth watch had ended. Cao Cao ordered his soldiers to pile bundles of straw around the camp and set them alight, while his officers raised a great clamor and charged straight in. At the time, Chunyu Qiong had just been drinking with his officers and lay drunk in his tent; hearing the uproar, he leapt up in haste and demanded, “What is all this commotion?” Before he had finished speaking, grappling hooks had already dragged him down. Sui Yuanjin and Zhao Rui were just returning from transporting grain. Seeing flames rise from the depot, they hurried to its aid. Cao Cao's soldiers rushed to report: “Enemy troops are behind us. Please divide the army to resist them.” Cao Cao shouted, “Every officer is to press forward with all his strength! Do not turn to fight until the enemy reaches our backs!” At this, every soldier and officer vied to be first in the assault. In an instant, flames rose on every side, and smoke obscured the sky. The two generals Sui and Zhao drove their troops forward to the rescue, and Cao Cao reined about to meet them. The two generals could not withstand him and were both slain by Cao Cao's troops; all the provisions and fodder were burned to ashes. Chunyu Qiong was captured and brought before Cao Cao. Cao Cao ordered his ears, nose, and fingers cut off, had him bound upon a horse, and sent him back to Yuan Shao's camp in disgrace.

p.src: Meanwhile, Yuan Shao was in his tent when word came that flames filled the northern sky. Realizing Wuchao had been lost, he hurried outside, summoned his civil and military officers, and consulted them about sending a relief force. Zhang He said, “Gao Lan and I will go together to its aid.” Guo Tu said, “No. Since Cao Cao's troops are raiding the grain, Cao Cao himself is certain to have gone with them. With Cao Cao away, his camp must be empty. We should send our troops to strike his camp first. When Cao Cao hears of it, he will surely hasten back. This is Sun Bin's stratagem of ‘besieging Wei to rescue Zhao.’” Zhang He said, “That is wrong. Cao Cao is full of schemes. Whenever he goes out, he is certain to leave defenses within against the unexpected. If we attack Cao Cao's camp now and fail to take it, while Chunyu Qiong and the others are captured, all of us will be taken prisoner.” Guo Tu said, “Cao Cao is intent only on seizing the grain. How could he have left troops in his camp?” Again and again, he urged an attack on Cao Cao's camp. Yuan Shao therefore sent Zhang He and Gao Lan with five thousand troops to attack Cao Cao's camp at Guandu, and sent Jiang Qi with ten thousand troops to relieve Wuchao.

p.src: Now Cao Cao, having scattered Chunyu Qiong's troops, seized all their armor and banners. His men disguised themselves as Chunyu Qiong's defeated soldiers returning to camp, and on a secluded mountain path they encountered Jiang Qi's force. When Jiang Qi's troops questioned them, they claimed to be defeated soldiers fleeing back from Wuchao. Jiang Qi suspected nothing and rode straight past. Suddenly Zhang Liao and Xu Chu appeared, shouting, “Jiang Qi, do not flee!” Taken wholly unprepared, Jiang Qi was struck from his horse and slain by Zhang Liao, and all his troops were destroyed. Cao Cao also sent a man ahead with the false report: “Jiang Qi has already scattered the troops attacking Wuchao.” Consequently, Yuan Shao sent no further force to aid Wuchao and merely reinforced the troops going to Guandu.

p.src: Meanwhile, as Zhang He and Gao Lan attacked Cao Cao's camp, Xiahou Dun charged from the left, Cao Ren from the right, and Cao Hong from the center. Struck from three directions at once, Yuan Shao's army suffered a crushing defeat. By the time Yuan Shao's reinforcements arrived, Cao Cao had also attacked from the rear, surrounding and slaughtering them on every side. Zhang He and Gao Lan fought their way free and escaped. Yuan Shao gathered the remnants of the defeated Wuchao force and returned to camp, where he saw Chunyu Qiong bereft of ears and nose, with his hands and feet mutilated. Yuan Shao asked, “How was Wuchao lost?” The defeated soldiers told him, “Chunyu Qiong lay drunk and was therefore unable to resist the enemy.”

p.src: Enraged, Yuan Shao had him beheaded on the spot. Guo Tu feared that Zhang He and Gao Lan would return to camp and dispute the rights and wrongs of the matter. He therefore slandered them before Yuan Shao first, saying, “Zhang He and Gao Lan must be rejoicing inwardly at my lord's defeat.” Yuan Shao said, “Why do you say that?” Guo Tu said, “Those two have long intended to surrender to Cao Cao. When sent to attack his camp, they deliberately refused to exert themselves, causing the loss of our soldiers.” Yuan Shao flew into a rage and dispatched a messenger to summon the two men back to camp at once to answer for their crimes. But Guo Tu first sent a man to tell them, “My lord means to kill you.” When Yuan Shao's messenger arrived, Gao Lan asked, “Why has my lord summoned us?” The messenger replied, “I do not know the reason.” Gao Lan immediately drew his sword and slew the messenger. Zhang He was greatly startled. Gao Lan said, “Yuan Shao believes slander and is certain to be captured by Cao Cao. How can we sit here waiting for death? We would do better to go and join Cao Cao.” Zhang He said, “I too have long had that thought.”

p.src: Thereupon the two men led the troops under their command to Cao Cao's camp and surrendered. Xiahou Dun said, “Zhang He and Gao Lan have come to surrender, but we do not yet know whether their intentions are genuine.” Cao Cao said, “I shall treat them with kindness. Even if they harbor other intentions, those too can be changed.” He therefore opened the camp gates and ordered the two men admitted. They reversed their spears, removed their armor, and prostrated themselves upon the ground. Cao Cao said, “Had Yuan Shao been willing to heed the counsel of you two generals, he would not have suffered defeat. Now that you two generals have chosen to join me, it is like Weizi leaving Yin or Han Xin giving his allegiance to Han.” He appointed Zhang He General of the Household and Marquis of Duting, and Gao Lan General of the Household and Marquis of Donglai. The two men were overjoyed.

p.src: Meanwhile, Yuan Shao had lost Xu You, then Zhang He and Gao Lan, and also the grain at Wuchao. The morale of his army was in turmoil. Xu You again urged Cao Cao to advance swiftly. Zhang He and Gao Lan asked to serve as the vanguard, and Cao Cao consented. He immediately ordered Zhang He and Gao Lan to lead troops in a raid upon Yuan Shao's camp. At the third watch that night, three columns set out to raid the camp. The confused battle raged until dawn, when each side withdrew its troops; Yuan Shao's army had lost more than half its men. Xun You offered a plan: “We should now spread word that our forces are being reassigned—one column to take Suanzao and attack Ye Commandery, and another to take Liyang and cut off Yuan Shao's army's road of retreat. When Yuan Shao hears this, he is sure to panic and divide his forces to oppose us. We shall strike while his troops are in motion, and Yuan Shao can then be defeated.”

p.src: Cao Cao adopted his plan and ordered officers and men throughout the army to spread the word far and wide. When Yuan Shao's troops heard the news, they reported at his camp, “Cao Cao has divided his army into two forces: one is advancing on Ye Commandery, and the other on Liyang.” Greatly alarmed, Yuan Shao hastily sent Yuan Shang with fifty thousand troops to relieve Ye Commandery and Xin Ming with another fifty thousand to relieve Liyang; they set out that very night. Learning that Yuan Shao's forces were on the move, Cao Cao divided his main army and sent eight columns charging straight at Yuan Shao's camp. Yuan Shao's troops had no will to fight; they scattered and fled, and the whole army collapsed. Yuan Shao had no time to don his armor and mounted his horse wearing only a plain robe and headcloth; his eldest son, Yuan Tan, followed behind him. The four generals Zhang Liao, Xu Chu, Xu Huang, and Yu Jin led their troops in pursuit of Yuan Shao. Yuan Shao hastily crossed the river, abandoning all his maps, documents, wagons, equipment, gold, silk, and valuables; he escaped with only the eight hundred-odd horsemen attending him.
